Heart Failure

The echocardiogram provided is not suggestive of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)*.

Disclaimer

* Based on the assumption that an apical four chamber echocardiogram with an ejection fraction ≥50% has been provided, HFpEF is defined as: (i) clinical signs and symptoms leading to clinical diagnosis of heart failure; (ii) an ejection fraction ≥50%; and (iii) evidence of elevated intra-cardiac filling pressures according to echocardiography. Please refer to the clinician’s manual for further information.

Device is indicated as a diagnostic aid. Patient management decisions should not be made solely on the results of the EchoGo Heart Failure 2.0 analysis.

EchoGo Score reflects an estimate of the likelihood that a patient has HFpEF. It does not reflect prevalence, which is the number of patients with HFpEF in a given population. EchoGo Score should be interpreted alongside other relevant clinical characteristics and patient testing.

Uncertainty is the width of the highlighted EchoGo Score bin. Wider bins indicate greater uncertainty; it is not a ± interval around the score.
